report_markdown:
**Content ideas for Ledgerly** 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-16
US relative search interest in “invoice fraud” reached its chart peak on November 13—not evidence that fraud incidents increased.

1. **Invoice-fraud search interest peaked—not necessarily invoice fraud** (search_trend, Nov 13)
   The supplied trends page shows relative interest of 100 of 100 on November 13, versus 57 on November 7, for the United States over its past-30-days chart. These values measure relative search interest, not search counts or fraud incidence.
   Ledgerly can explain the limits of this attention signal without offering fraud-prevention advice or asserting an increase in losses.
   Post to write: A newsletter section, “Invoice fraud is trending: what the chart actually tells finance teams,” separating relative search interest from incident rates and losses. [source](https://trends.example/explore?q=invoice+fraud&geo=US&date=past-30-days)

2. **PayFlow’s 80% replacement claim needs its survey context** (report, Nov 13)
   PayFlow’s vendor survey, published November 13, says 80% of 200 surveyed CFOs plan to replace their AP software in 2027. The supplied page gives no fieldwork dates, geography, company sizes or recruitment methods.
   Ledgerly can explain why this is not a representative finding about mid-size US companies and identify the questions the headline leaves unanswered.
   Post to write: A LinkedIn post, “Before you repeat the 80% AP replacement headline,” identifying the vendor source, missing methodology and questions the figure leaves unanswered. [source](https://payflow.example/blog/cfo-survey)

3. **E-invoice framework v2 adds credit notes and partial payments** (regulation, Nov 12)
   The Business Payments Coalition’s November 12 announcement describes a common invoice-exchange format between US businesses’ accounting systems. Version 2 adds credit notes and partial payments and takes effect for participating networks on March 1, 2027.
   Explain the announced scope and its connection to AP workflows. Link readers to the standard body; do not present participation as a universal US legal requirement or imply Ledgerly compatibility.
   Post to write: A blog post, “E-invoice framework v2: what changed and who it affects,” explaining credit notes, partial payments and the participating-network effective date. [source](https://bpc.example/news/e-invoicing-framework-v2-final)

4. **Controller Pulse puts invoice exceptions at the late-close bottleneck** (report, Nov 10)
   Controller Pulse 2026 reports that 61% of 840 surveyed controllers at US companies with $50M–$1B revenue identify invoice exceptions—price or quantity mismatches—as the main cause of a late close. Published November 10; fielded September 8–26, 2026.
   Ledgerly can map exception ownership and resolution across AP workflows, moving beyond its existing introductory matching content without promising close-time improvements.
   Post to write: A carousel, “Where invoice exceptions stall the close,” tracing a price or quantity mismatch through detection, ownership, resolution and approval. [source](https://fpa-association.example/research/controller-pulse-2026)

_Plan ahead: E-invoice exchange framework v2 takes effect for participating networks on March 1, 2027. [Announcement](https://bpc.example/news/e-invoicing-framework-v2-final)._

Evidence note: These ideas rely on the supplied page snapshots. Independent corroboration was unavailable. No earlier-edition hooks were supplied for repeat checking.
